## 1. Introduction

Gas turbine engine is a critical machinery system with complex structure, high integration and poor working conditions, and its reliable and efficient operation is crucial to the safety of the flight [1]. The engine performance is gradually degraded in the entire life cycle due to fouling, erosion of blades and seals, blade tip clearance [2,3]. The performance deterioration will inevitably cause the aircraft engine thrust loss, and additional fuel would be asked to maintain the required engine thrust. This also causes the engine move to the surge margin and increase exhaust gas temperature (EGT) [4]. In order to enhance the reliability of aircraft engine and reduce the costs of maintenance, condition based maintenance (CBM) is introduced to avoid unnecessary maintenance and facilitating mission scheduling. The CBM system consists of two typical parts: fault diagnostics and prognostics [5]. The main task of diagnostics is fault detection, identification and isolation. Prognostics is responsible for performance prediction, and its primary objective is to estimate how much remaining useful time (RUL) is available

Online sequential extreme learning machine (OS-ELM) learns data one-by-one or chunk-by-chunk, and the recursive least square (RLS) algorithm is commonly employed to train the topological parameters of OS-ELM. Since it is hard to guarantee the smallest estimation error of the state variable by the RLS, the regression performance of the OS-ELM easily fl uctuates in practical applications. To address this gap, a new training approach of the OS-ELM using Kalman fi lter called KFOS-ELM is proposed, and state propagation is combined into extreme learning process to obtain the OS-ELM's topological parameters. Besides, an adaptive-weighted ensemble mechanism is developed and used to dynamically tune the weight coefficients of each KFOS-ELM in the learning network. The regression performance of the proposed methodology is evaluated using benchmark datasets. The simulation results show that proposed methods are superior to the OS-ELM and EOS-ELM in terms of the regression accuracy and stability without additional computational efforts. Furthermore, an enhanced multi-sensor prognostic model based on KFOS-ELM and logistic regression (LR) model is designed for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of aircraft engine. The experimental results confirm our viewpoints.

The quantifiable engine performance degradation is the key to condition-based maintenance. From the economic affordability, reliable health assessments and prognostics can effectively reduce life cycle costs and improve engine reliability as well as availability [6,7]. Moreover, prognostics in gas turbine engine can be properly utilized for maintenance to recover the health condition before failure, thus avoids the occurrence of catastrophic accidents. The existing engine prognostics methods are generally classified into two categories: model-based methods and data-driven methods. Model-based methods normally require to build mathematical models to estimate the physical characteristics of engine failure modes. However, the engine failure process is usually complicated, and it is hard to own an engine dynamic model with high confidence in the whole operating range for health prognostics. Recently, the data-driven methods attract more attention with the rapid development of learning machine and the increasing accumulation of fl ight data [8]. In addition, some typical data-driven methods have been successfully developed for engine health prognostics and RUL prediction [9-11]. Data-driven methods are capable of improving accuracy of RUL prediction without additional physical theorization of the engine in the event of proper utilization.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The common data-driven methods generally involve statistical data characteristics, artificial neural networks (ANNs), support vector machine (SVM), evolutionary prognostics, fuzzy logic, etc. [12-14]. ANNs have been rapidly developed in the fi elds of fault diagnosis and health prognostics due to its effective nonlinear mapping abilities. Yuan et al. [15] discussed long short-term memory (LSTM) network for aero-engine fault diagnosis and RUL prediction. Janssens et al. [16] presented convolutional neural network based fault detection for rotating machinery. Bing and Qu [17] introduced the stacked denoising auto-encoder (SDA) to solve the aero-engine sensor fault diagnosis problem. The basic ANNs, such as feed-forward neural networks and radial basis function networks, are usually composed of input layer, hidden layer and output layer [18,19]. The gradient based training approaches are extensively utilized to train neural networks and the parameters of neural networks are tuned iteratively, which leads to slow learning speed in practical application. To reduce the network parameters, extreme learning machine (ELM) is developed from single hidden layer feed-forward neural network (SLFNs) [20], and its improved types are applied in several fi elds [21,22]. Unlike those traditional neural networks, ELM randomly chooses the input weights and analytically determines the output weights. The learning speed of ELM is faster than traditional feed-forward networks, at the same time it obtains better generalization performance.

For online sequential learning problems, the OS-ELM algorithm is proposed based on the recursive least square (RLS) [23,24]. Compared to other well-known sequential learning algorithms, OS-ELM presents better generalization performance and less training time consumption, but it is easy to fl uctuate to topological parameters. Neural network ensemble technique is addressed to make up for the instability deficiency. Lan et al. [25] proposed an ensemble of online sequential extreme learning machine (EOS-ELM), and the output of EOS-ELM is an average of several OS-ELMs. However, some individuals among those OS-ELMs might have lower regression accuracy, and they are treated the same as other OSELM individual in the networks. Besides, the least square of the estimation output errors is commonly utilized as the objective of ELM training strategy, while the least covariance of the state estimates rather than output errors leads to the optimal state variable in the linear estimation sense [26,27]. Kalman fi lter (KF) is a wellknown state estimation algorithm, and it relies on recursive linear minimum covariance estimation. State estimates at the next step is calculated from the current state variable with the posteriori measurement correction in the KF algorithm.

This paper proposes a novel KF-based learning algorithm to online sequentially update topological parameters of the ELM called KFOS-ELM, and then applies it for aircraft engine degradation prognostics. KFOS-ELM treats the output weights as state variables to be estimated by KF propagation. The state covariance from measurement error is minimized, and utilized to update output weights of the KFOS-ELM at each step. In addition, a bank of KFOS-ELMs is developed from the ensemble OS-ELM, where each KFOS-ELM individual runs parallel. A weight coefficient vector of the adaptive-weighted ensemble of KFOS-ELM (AEKFOS-ELM) is introduced to weight off the contribution to the network output of every individual network. The coefficient vector tunes to the regression accuracy of each individual at the latest several steps in the network. The performance comparisons of the involved OSELMs are carried out using benchmark data in MATLAB environment. The following research is mainly undertaken by the authors both at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing, China, and at the University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada. The simulation results show that both of the proposed KFOS-ELM and AEKFOS-ELM produce better regression stability and accuracy than their plain OS-ELMs. AEKFOS-ELM obviously owns better regression performance than KFOS-ELM but consuming additional computational time. Finally, the RUL estimation of aircraft engine is presented by the combination of AEKFOS-ELM and logistic regression (LR) model, and its effectiveness is assessed on NASA engine degradation datasets.

The roadmap of this paper is as follows. In section 2, KF learning mechanism is introduced to the calculation of OS-ELM topological parameters. The adaptive-weight ensemble KFOS-ELM algorithm is developed from the previous studies, the framework and procedure of which are followed in detail in section 3. Section 4 gives the systematic comparisons of the OS-ELM, KFOS-ELM, EOSELM and AEKFOS-ELM on benchmark datasets to the regression issue. The proposed algorithms are then applied to aircraft engine RUL estimation, and the test results and discussion are presented in section 5. Conclusions are drawn in section 6.

## 2.3. KFOS-ELM algorithm

Different from the basic ELM's training strategy of minimizing the least square of the estimation output errors, the proposed KF training strategy leads to the optimal state variable by minimizing the least covariance of the state estimates. The KF state propagation is introduced to recursively estimate the topological parameters of the KFOS-ELM with the posteriori measurement correction at each step. The proposed KFOS-ELM utilizes KF algorithm to estimate the output weights of OS-ELM without changing the network structure, and it learns sequential data in the chunk-bychunk mode. The schematic diagram of proposed KFOS-ELM is depicted in Fig. 1.

The initialization process of KFOS-ELM is the same as that of the plain OS-ELM, and a small data chunk is utilized to initially compute the matrix H 0 and output weight matrix β 0 . The output weights taken as the KF state variables are updated as new sample data chunk comes. We define β k | k - 1 = ⌢ β k - 1 + ξ as the prior estimation of output weights at k -th step, ⌢ β k - 1 denotes the output weight vector at ( k - 1)-th step, and ξ is the process noise. ## 3.1. Ensemble of OS-ELM

The main innovation of the EOS-ELM lies in the introduction of ensemble ideas into the online sequential learning model. Statistically speaking, the population average will be closer to the expectation than the elements in the population, and the EOS-ELM output is less fl uctuant than OS-ELM individuals in the network. The EOS-ELM introduces a population size parameter p , and the mean output approaches to its expectation with the increase of p . In the traditional EOS-ELM, each OS-ELM individual plays the same role in the network output, and the weight coefficient of each individual is 1/ p . That is to say, the EOS-ELM will be more stable as p becomes larger. However, the topological complexity increases along p increase, followed by the dramatically more computational time consumed. Hence, it is necessary to determine individual weight coefficient under the limited topological size in the ensemble architecture from two aspects of network training errors and computational efforts.

## 3.2. AEKFOS-ELM algorithm

## 4. Benchmark datasets test

In this section, the regression performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated using the benchmark datasets from UCI repository [32]. The involved online sequential regression algorithms include the OS-ELM, EOS-ELM, KFOS-ELM and AEKFOS-ELM. Monte Carlo simulation is carried out, and 50 trials are given in the test. The examined datasets contain Auto-MPG, Housing, Airfoil Self-Noise, Mackey-Glass, and Abalone. Their specifications of the attribute number (#Attribute), the number training samples (#Train), the number of testing samples (#Test) are shown in Table 1. The input data are normalized into the closed interval [- 1 , 1 ] , and target output into [ 0 , 1 ] . In order to reveal the learning evolution of the involved four algorithms, the test results are presented on Auto-MPG case using sigmoid activation function in Fig. 3 and RBF activation function in Fig. 4 (the number of training samples vs. RMSE ).

From Fig. 3(a) and Fig. 4(a), SD s of OS-ELM and KFOS-ELM are 0.0028 and 0.0019 on sigmoid activation function, and 0.0087 and 0.0024 on RBF activation function in the hidden layer for AutoMPG case. We can see that the evolution curves of the KFOS-ELM are smoother than OS-ELM. Moreover, KFOS-ELM's RMSE convergences to its steady terminal faster than that of OS-ELM, and less training samples are used to reach the same regression errors. In order to further evaluate the proposed prognostic methodologies, a turbofan engine performance degradation dataset generated by Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) [33] is utilized. In this study, the engine health performance prognostics is presented based on the proposed KFOS-ELM using multiple sensor data. ## 6. Conclusions

This paper has proposed a novel online sequential learning strategy for the OS-ELM algorithm, which utilizes KF state propagation to obtain the topological parameters of network. Unlike the plain OS-ELM methods, the proposed algorithms use KF algorithm to estimate the network output weights. Moreover, an adaptiveweighted ensemble of KFOS-ELM is developed from the EOS-ELM to improve the learning stability. It is a novel attempt to adopt the KF instead of traditional RLS in the training behavior. The methodology is tested and validated using regression benchmark data sets of the UCI repository. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the KFOS-ELM and AEKFOS-ELM achieve better regression accuracy and stability.

In addition, we presented a prognostic model for RUL estimation of aircraft engine by the combination of the proposed algorithms and LR model. The KFOS-ELM and AEKFOS-ELM algorithms are employed to predict feature parameters in an iterative manner. The LR model is used to determine the health indicator of the degrading aircraft engine. The experimental results on the degradation datasets obtained by the C-AMPSS indicate that the proposed methodology has better prediction performance. However, there are still several important topics for future research that are related to this work. Firstly, KFOS-ELMs yield a fi xed hidden neurons feedforward network. In order to weight off the regression accuracy and computational efforts, a self-tuning hidden neurons seems to be a better choice. Secondly, the evaluation of the proposed methodology is limited to the numerical simulation, and it will be of more practical significance of examine these involved algorithms on semi-physical hardware in loop simulation experiment.
